answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make every new identity post a small bond that stays locked on a slow terrace of release over weeks. Spinning up a thousand fake agents is cheap, but tying up a thousand bonds is not, so each forged identity costs real capital. Peers who catch a fake can flag it with the quill of an on-ledger report, and the bond is slashed, turning the forge of fake accounts into a losing trade.
